headline: High-risk default workspace overlap: Devin can write shared integrations and files, while AutoGPT can execute shell and access the filesystem, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-action risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A can read and act on filesystem content, and B can write files plus use MCP and shared integrations. That creates a plausible instruction-smuggling path if B writes attacker-controlled content into shared artifacts that A later ingests. The pair lacks documented provenance controls, so uncertainty stays at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF Devin writes attacker-controlled text into a shared repo, doc, or MCP-backed artifact that AutoGPT later reads as instructions.
IF AutoGPT is configured to treat file contents as trusted task input without provenance checks.
mitigations: Restrict AutoGPT to read-only access on shared workspaces.
Disable MCP or shared-integrations writes for Devin in paired runs.
Add a provenance header check before AutoGPT consumes any file.
Use separate workspaces for each agent.
requires-engineering: add content-signing or allowlist-based ingestion gates.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Devin touches source code, docs, issue trackers, and team chat, and can write to GitHub, Slack, Jira, and Notion with broad network egress. AutoGPT can execute shell and access the filesystem. If they share any workspace or handoff channel, sensitive content can flow from Devin into AutoGPT outputs or external APIs without a strong default barrier.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository, cloud workspace, or copied artifacts containing secrets or internal docs.
IF Devin's integration writes are visible to AutoGPT or AutoGPT can exfiltrate read files through its network egress.
mitigations: Keep separate repos/workspaces for the pair.
Remove secrets from shared files before handoff.
Disable Devin write scopes during paired runs.
Run AutoGPT with network egress blocked except approved endpoints.
requires-engineering: add DLP scanning on shared artifacts.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write to files and run shell commands; Devin also modifies git state and supports parallel sessions with shared integrations. AutoGPT has filesystem and shell access but no multiple-instance support, so concurrent edits to the same repo or workspace can race and corrupt state. The overlap is dangerous by default when paired on shared mutable resources.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same git checkout or cloud workspace.
IF Devin uses GitHub/Slack/Jira/Notion integrations while AutoGPT edits the same files locally.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate checkout.
Serialize file and git writes with a lock file.
Disable Devin git-write actions during AutoGPT runs.
Use branch-per-agent workflows.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level mutual exclusion.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Devin is an autonomous planner-executor that can act on GitHub, Slack, Jira, and Notion, while AutoGPT can generate shell actions and file edits. If Devin treats AutoGPT output as authoritative, a mistaken or injected result can cascade into commits, tickets, or messages. The pair lacks documented verification gates, so the safer severity is high.
conditions: IF Devin consumes AutoGPT-produced text as facts or instructions without a verification step.
IF Devin uses that output to create commits, tickets, or messages through its write integrations.
mitigations: Require human review before Devin acts on AutoGPT output.
Add a verification checklist for all AutoGPT-derived claims.
Limit Devin to draft-only mode in paired runs.
Tag AutoGPT outputs as untrusted in the handoff channel.
requires-engineering: enforce schema-validated handoffs.

E_compliance.rationale: Devin is closed-source, cloud-hosted, and handles repo deploy keys and integration tokens across GitHub, Slack, Jira, and Notion; AutoGPT is open-source and filesystem-oriented. The profiles do not specify a direct residency or certification mismatch, but the pair can move internal code and chat data into a vendor-managed workspace, creating a plausible policy mismatch that is not mitigated by default.
conditions: IF regulated or internal data is placed into Devin's cloud workspace or integrations.
IF the organization requires residency, retention, or certification guarantees not documented for the paired workflow.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair.
Review vendor DPA and retention settings before use.
Disable Slack/Jira/Notion writes for sensitive projects.
Use synthetic or redacted data in paired runs.
requires-engineering: route regulated workloads to a compliant environment.
